Introducing Technova ​

About Technova ​

Welcome to Technova, a fictional technology retail company that sells a variety of technology products, including laptops, smartphones, monitors, computer accessories, and networking equipment.

Like any growing business, Technova needs a way to manage its products, customers, orders, payments, suppliers, employees, and inventory.

To support these operations, Technova uses a relational database built with Microsoft SQL Server.

Throughout SQL Power Hour, you'll work with Technova's database to solve practical problems using SQL. Each topic introduces a set of questions based on the same database, allowing you to apply what you've learned in a consistent, realistic environment.

Understanding the Database ​

Technova's database consists of 11 tables. Each table represents a particular entity or concept within the business.

The tables are related through primary keys and foreign keys, allowing us to retrieve and analyze information across the database.

The following sections describe each table, its columns, and the information stored in each column.

Note: PK identifies a primary key, while FK identifies a foreign key referencing another table. These labels are included in the descriptions for clarity.

Nullability: A column marked NULL in its data type may contain missing values. Every other column is required and always has a value.

Naming Conventions ​

All table and column names use snake_case: lowercase words separated by underscores, such as order_items and customer_id. Table names are plural.

Because the names are lowercase, you can write them in your queries without double quotes:

sql
SELECT customer_id, first_name
FROM customers;

To inspect a table's structure at any time in psql, use \d followed by the table name, for example \d products. Use \dt to list all tables.

1. categories ​

The categories table stores the categories into which Technova organizes its products.

Examples include Laptops, Smartphones, Monitors, Accessories, and Networking Equipment.

Column NameData TypeDescription
category_idINTEGERPrimary key. Uniquely identifies each category.
category_nameVARCHAR(100)Name of the product category.
descriptionVARCHAR(255), NULLBrief description of the category, if provided.

2. suppliers ​

The suppliers table stores information about the companies that supply products to Technova.

Column NameData TypeDescription
supplier_idINTEGERPrimary key. Uniquely identifies each supplier.
supplier_nameVARCHAR(150)Name of the supplier company.
contact_emailVARCHAR(150)Supplier's contact email address.
countryVARCHAR(100), NULLCountry in which the supplier operates, if known.

3. products ​

The products table stores information about the products Technova offers for sale.

Each product belongs to a category and has a primary supplier.

Column NameData TypeDescription
product_idINTEGERPrimary key. Uniquely identifies each product.
product_nameVARCHAR(150)Name of the product.
category_idINTEGERForeign key referencing categories. Identifies the product's category.
supplier_idINTEGERForeign key referencing suppliers. Identifies the product's primary supplier.
unit_priceNUMERIC(10,2)Current selling price of one unit of the product.
cost_priceNUMERIC(10,2)Cost to Technova of acquiring one unit of the product.
created_atDATEDate the product was added to Technova's catalog.

4. customers ​

The customers table stores information about people who purchase products from Technova.

Column NameData TypeDescription
customer_idINTEGERPrimary key. Uniquely identifies each customer.
first_nameVARCHAR(100)Customer's first name.
last_nameVARCHAR(100)Customer's last name.
emailVARCHAR(150)Customer's email address. Unique: no two customers share an email.
cityVARCHAR(100)City in which the customer resides.
countryVARCHAR(100)Country in which the customer resides.
registered_atDATEDate the customer registered with Technova.

5. departments ​

The departments table stores information about Technova's organizational departments.

Examples include Sales, Customer Support, Logistics, IT, and Finance.

Column NameData TypeDescription
department_idINTEGERPrimary key. Uniquely identifies each department.
department_nameVARCHAR(100)Name of the department.
locationVARCHAR(100), NULLLocation associated with the department, if any.

6. employees ​

The employees table stores information about people working at Technova.

Each employee belongs to a department and may be assigned responsibility for handling customer orders.

Column NameData TypeDescription
employee_idINTEGERPrimary key. Uniquely identifies each employee.
first_nameVARCHAR(100)Employee's first name.
last_nameVARCHAR(100)Employee's last name.
department_idINTEGERForeign key referencing departments. Identifies the employee's department.
hire_dateDATEDate the employee joined Technova.
job_titleVARCHAR(100)Employee's job title.

7. orders ​

The orders table stores information about orders placed by Technova's customers.

Each order belongs to a customer and may be assigned to an employee.

Column NameData TypeDescription
order_idINTEGERPrimary key. Uniquely identifies each order.
customer_idINTEGERForeign key referencing customers. Identifies the customer who placed the order.
employee_idINTEGER, NULLForeign key referencing employees. Identifies the employee responsible for the order, if assigned.
order_dateDATEDate the order was placed.
order_statusVARCHAR(30)Current status of the order. One of: Pending, Processing, Shipped, Delivered, or Cancelled.

8. order_items ​

The order_items table stores the individual products included in each order.

An order can contain multiple products, and a product can appear in multiple orders. This table records the relationship between orders and products.

Column NameData TypeDescription
order_item_idINTEGERPrimary key. Uniquely identifies each order item.
order_idINTEGERForeign key referencing orders. Identifies the order containing the item.
product_idINTEGERForeign key referencing products. Identifies the product purchased.
quantityINTEGERNumber of units of the product included in the order. Always greater than zero.
unit_priceNUMERIC(10,2)Price per unit at the time the order was placed.

Important: The unit_price in this table represents the historical purchase price, whereas products.unit_price represents the current selling price. These values may differ.

9. payments ​

The payments table records payments associated with customer orders.

An order may have multiple payment records, allowing Technova to track payments made through separate transactions.

Column NameData TypeDescription
payment_idINTEGERPrimary key. Uniquely identifies each payment record.
order_idINTEGERForeign key referencing orders. Identifies the order associated with the payment.
payment_dateDATEDate the payment was recorded.
amountNUMERIC(10,2)Monetary amount of the payment.
payment_methodVARCHAR(30)Method used to make the payment. One of: Card, PayPal, or Bank Transfer.
payment_statusVARCHAR(30)Status of the payment. One of: Pending, Completed, or Failed.

10. warehouses ​

The warehouses table stores information about the locations where Technova keeps its inventory.

Column NameData TypeDescription
warehouse_idINTEGERPrimary key. Uniquely identifies each warehouse.
warehouse_nameVARCHAR(100)Name of the warehouse.
cityVARCHAR(100)City in which the warehouse is located.
countryVARCHAR(100)Country in which the warehouse is located.

11. inventory ​

The inventory table tracks the quantity of each product stored at individual warehouses.

A product may be stored in multiple warehouses, and each warehouse may store multiple products. Each product has at most one inventory record per warehouse.

Column NameData TypeDescription
inventory_idINTEGERPrimary key. Uniquely identifies each inventory record.
product_idINTEGERForeign key referencing products. Identifies the product being tracked.
warehouse_idINTEGERForeign key referencing warehouses. Identifies the warehouse storing the product.
quantity_in_stockINTEGERNumber of units currently available in the warehouse.
reorder_levelINTEGERStock threshold below which replenishment should be considered.
last_updatedDATEDate the inventory record was last updated.

Summary ​

Technova's database contains 11 tables covering four main areas of the business:

AreaTablesPurpose
Product Catalogcategories, suppliers, productsOrganizes products and their suppliers.
Customers & Salescustomers, orders, order_items, paymentsTracks customers, purchases, and payments.
Inventorywarehouses, inventoryTracks stock across warehouse locations.
Company Operationsdepartments, employeesRepresents Technova's internal organization.

As you work through SQL Power Hour, you'll use these tables to practise retrieving, filtering, sorting, grouping, joining, and analyzing data.

The same database will support increasingly challenging exercises, allowing you to build on your existing knowledge and develop stronger SQL problem-solving skills.
